quorum.rounds: one round of three lanes at cdd03571 with the base pinned at 0c1277c6, judging both tickets together. Two lanes returned FAIL; one returned no structured output and is recorded rather than dropped. Nine of twelve claims confirmed by both returning lanes.
quorum.kill_rule: the brief named the attack rather than hoping a lane would find it: could the soft switch leak from a caller's environment into a gate run? Both returning lanes answered yes, independently. The hole was closed one commit later — the switch is the third positional argument now, which cannot be inherited — and no_environment_variable_can_soften_the_gate pins it. One round for two tickets is deliberate: three lanes each would have cost six lanes to judge nine changed lines, and batching is the only way to spend less without lowering a floor.
refuted_claims: The soft switch was readable from the environment (`${DOGFOOD_WINDOW_SOFT:-0}`), refuted by both returning lanes independently: an operator exporting that name in a shell profile would soften every gate that sources the library, silently. Corrected at 50073b89 — it is the third positional argument of dogfood_prs_between, passed by show and by nothing else — with a case that runs gate T with the name exported and asserts a real verdict and no degraded line.

As worded: 'nothing else in that function changes' — refuted by one lane, because PMAT-229's soft path is in the same function. The claim meant 'nothing else about the census output' and said it badly; the receipts now state that the two tickets share dogfood_prs_between.

As worded: 'docs/audits/logs/PMAT-228-gate-tests.log records both RED cases' — refuted by both lanes: the file did not exist at the commit they judged. It was written at the next commit with --no-fail-fast, because an earlier run had stopped at the first failing binary and left one red case unmeasured. The same error as PMAT-231's row count and the same fix: measure the commit, not the moment.
lane_errors: Lane 1 returned no structured output. The round is three lanes wide on paper and two in evidence, and every confirmed claim rests on two independent re-runs rather than three.

crux.verdict: accept(all four surveyed systems separate the machine-readable result of a command from the human-readable narration of it — Terraform's -json plan against its rendered plan, Ansible's callback plugins against the JSON result object, kubectl's -o json against its table, nix build's --json against its progress bar — and in all four the narration goes to the stream the machine does not read [X]. forjar had one function writing both to stdout, and a caller that captured it wrote a narration line into a data file [V]. The second half has no direct analogue: none of the four has a status command that shares a gate's predicate, because none of them has this repository's rule that an unmeasured check is a failing one. Rendering the measurable part while failing on the rest is the shape that rule implies, and it is why the exit code did not move.)
